title: CRLR/218/2012 of KRISHNA BAHADUR LAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.218 of 2012
Krishna Bahadur Lal
ÖÖÖ..Revisionist
Versus
State of Uttarakhand
ÖÖÖRespondent
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 Mr. J.M. Sharma, Advocate, for the revisionist.
 Mr. K.S. Rautela, A.G.A., for the State.
Having heard learned counsel for the revisionist, nay the
State counsel, it appears that the first information report was
lodged against the revisionist on 12.1.2005, the investigation
in pursuance whereof resulted into the submission of
chargesheet on 9.12.2005 for the offences under Sections
420/423 IPC against him. It further appears that the
revisionist thereafter filed the C482 petition no.380/2006
before this Court seeking to quash the said chargesheet, which
was dismissed on 6.3.2012, wherein the entire merits as well
as the arguments raised by learned counsel for revisionist for
quashing of chargesheet, were considered in detail, but the
Court did not find any substance therein and accordingly,
ordered for commencement of trial. Subsequently thereafter,
the revisionist filed a special leave petition before the Apex
Court, which too met with the same fate of dismissal on
5.6.2012.
Subsequently thereafter, revisionist moved an application
before the concerned Magistrate seeking his discharge u/s 239
Cr.P.C. and also praying for exemption from his personal
attendance in the court u/s 205 Cr.P.C. After hearing the
arguments of accused, the court below has rejected both the

2
applications, moved u/s 205 Cr.P.C. and also u/s 239 Cr.P.C.,
and granted twenty daysí time to the revisionist to surrender,
and in case of failure, it was directed that the coercive
measures will be adopted against him for ensuring his
attendance.
Before this Court, learned counsel for the revisionist,
while referring to the provisions of Sections 227, 239 and 240
Cr.P.C., has argued that the impugned order is not
sustainable in the eyes of law.
Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case,
the Court do not agree with the said argument and feels that
the accused is defying every process of law by taking recourse
to one provision or the other, but is not prepared to surrender
in the court in pursuance of the chargesheet submitted
against him for the offences under Sections 420/423 IPC. All
the more, revisionist is not permitting the court below to level
charge against him for last seven years. Needless to mention
that this Court, while dismissing the petition moved by the
revisionist u/s 482 Cr.P.C., has already considered each and
every aspect of the matter, as also the arguments put forth on
behalf of accused for quashing of the charge sheet. But when
the revisionist failed before this Court and also before the Apex
Court, then he moved application under Sections 205/239
Cr.P.C. seeking exemption from his personal attendance as
well as for his discharge, and that too, without putting his
personal appearance or surrendering before the court, for the
offences, wherefor he has been charge-sheeted.
This Court, after analyzing the impugned order dated
8.10.2012 passed by the court below, in great detail, finds that
no valid infirmity or illegality could be pointed out in the same
by learned counsel. This revision, filed under Sections
397/401 Cr.P.C., is a gross abuse of process of court and

3
more so, when the same could have been filed before the
Sessions Judge itself. Thus, the Court dismisses the revision
in limine by imposing costs of Rs.10,000/- again the revisionist
for abusing the process of law for a number of times, and
failing to surrender before the court below. The costs will be
deposited in the government funds.
Let a copy of this order be sent to the court concerned,
which shall ensure the realization of costs. However, it is
made clear that the court below, while disposing of the bail
application on merits, will not prejudice with the costs, so
imposed by this Court.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
17.10.2012
Rd an g
